About

I'm Tia — based in London, drawn to things that cross boundaries. I've spent years helping people navigate some of the biggest transitions of their lives: where to study, how to migrate, what comes next. That work taught me to read complexity, tell stories, and see systems from the inside.

Now I'm applying that same attention to a different kind of transition. I'm not a technologist, but I'm genuinely fascinated by what's happening in AI and robotics — not the hype, but the actual questions. What does it mean for a machine to act in the physical world? What kind of identity should an AI agent have?

I'm also a founder. Nexart started with the idea that art and technology should be in the same room, and that the people making art — especially women in places where opportunity is scarce — deserved better infrastructure. That's still the core of it.

02

AI & Robotics

What I'm paying attention to. Updated as I learn.

I'm not an engineer. But I watch closely — following the people building things, reading what I can, and trying to understand what's actually changing, not just what's being announced.

Directions I find genuinely interesting
Embodied AI
Robots that operate in the real world, not just digital environments. The gap between language and physical grounding is where the hard problems live — and where I think the most interesting things will happen.
AI agent identity
As agents become more capable, the question of how they represent themselves — and how we verify that — becomes urgent. This is connected to why I filed a patent with Nexart around this idea.
Foundation models for robotics
The idea that a single model could learn to control many different robots — generalizing across hardware the way language models generalize across tasks. Following what's being built at NVIDIA, Physical Intelligence, and Figure.
People I follow
Jim Fan
Senior research scientist at NVIDIA. Working on foundation models for robotics — the kind of generalization that would make a robot as flexible as a language model.
Andrej Karpathy
Makes the inside of AI systems legible to people who weren't trained as ML engineers. The way he explains things is rare.
Following on X
Tracking researchers, founders, and observers across embodied AI, agent systems, and where art meets machine intelligence. Always looking for people who think carefully rather than loudly.
03

Nexart

A project I started. Still in motion.

Nexart started with a simple frustration: the infrastructure connecting artists to collectors — especially women artists in places where opportunity is limited — was broken, or absent entirely. The original idea was to use NFTs as a bridge: a way for a weaver in a remote community to have provable ownership of her work and access to a global market.

The NFT market moved in ways that made that harder. But while watching the space closely, I noticed something else: as AI agents become more capable, the question of identity becomes critical. How does an agent prove it is who it says it is? How do you give an AI a verifiable, unique identity that persists across contexts?

NFTs are actually well-suited to this — they're designed for exactly this kind of provable uniqueness. So Nexart evolved. I drafted a patent around AI agent identity and filed it in the UK. It's pending. The infrastructure question is still unsolved — but the idea feels more relevant now than when I started.

04

Film

Films that left something behind.

I watch across genres — the one consistent thread is films that make the impossible feel inevitable, or the familiar feel strange. Basically everything except horror.

Interstellar
Nolan · 2014
Time as a physical dimension you can move through. The tesseract scene is the most honest attempt I've seen at making the incomprehensible visible — and still emotional.
Sci-fi
Inception
Nolan · 2010
About the architecture of belief. A constructed reality can feel completely real if it's consistent enough — I think about this more now that I work near AI.
Thriller
The Lord of the Rings
Jackson · 2001–03
The standard for what commitment to a vision looks like. Everything has weight, history, consequence. Raised the bar for world-building permanently.
Epic
Spirited Away
Miyazaki · 2001
A world with completely different rules that you accept within minutes. The best films don't explain their logic — they just make you believe it.
Animation
